explanation: Correct answer: which. Which introduces a relative clause referring to a thing and acts as the subject of explains. That would also be possible but is not among the options.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun for a person acting as the object.
anchor: The journalist ___ we interviewed yesterday was very friendly.
explanation: Correct answer: whom. Whom is the formal object form used for people. Who would also be common in informal English but is not among the options. Whose indicates possession.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after a preposition.
anchor: The colleague to ___ I sent the report has replied.
explanation: Correct answer: whom. In formal English whom is used for people after a preposition. The construction to whom is grammatically correct. Who is not normally used immediately after a fronted preposition in formal English.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after a preposition referring to a thing.
anchor: The project on ___ we are working is confidential.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Which refers to things and can follow a preposition in formal relative clauses. On which is equivalent to which we are working on in less formal English.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun expressing possession.
anchor: She is the scientist ___ research changed the field.
explanation: Correct answer: whose. Whose introduces a possessive relationship between the scientist and her research. It can be used for people and also for things.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a defining clause.
anchor: The students ___ passed the exam received certificates.
explanation: Correct answer: who. Who is the subject of passed. Whom is an object form and cannot replace the subject here. Whose expresses possession.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a defining clause.
anchor: Everything ___ he said was true.
explanation: Correct answer: that. That is the standard relative pronoun after everything in a defining relative clause. Who and whom refer to people and where refers to places.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after a superlative.
anchor: This is the most interesting film ___ I have ever seen.
explanation: Correct answer: that. That is commonly preferred after superlatives in defining relative clauses. The pronoun could also be omitted because it functions as an object.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after the word only.
anchor: She is the only person ___ knows the password.
explanation: Correct answer: who. Who acts as the subject of knows and refers to a person. That is also possible in a defining clause but is not among the options.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun for an object.
anchor: The documents ___ you requested are ready.
explanation: Correct answer: that. That can refer to things in defining relative clauses. It functions as the object of requested and could also be omitted.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun for a person.
anchor: The people ___ live upstairs are very noisy.
explanation: Correct answer: who. Who acts as the subject of live. Whom is an object form. Whose indicates possession and which normally refers to things.

prompt: Choose the correct relative word for a location.
anchor: The village ___ my grandparents live is very small.
explanation: Correct answer: where. Where refers to the location in which the grandparents live. When refers to time and why to reason.

prompt: Choose the correct pronoun in a non-defining relative clause.
anchor: My father, ___ is sixty years old, still runs marathons.
explanation: Correct answer: who. Non-defining relative clauses add extra information and are separated by commas. Who refers to people. That cannot be used in non-defining relative clauses.

prompt: Choose the correct pronoun in a non-defining relative clause.
anchor: My car, ___ I bought last year, has already broken down.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Which refers to a thing in a non-defining relative clause. That is not allowed in non-defining relative clauses.

prompt: Choose the correct pronoun in a non-defining relative clause.
anchor: Prague, ___ is the capital of the Czech Republic, attracts many tourists.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Which acts as the subject of is and refers to the city. Where cannot act as the subject of is in this structure. That is not used in non-defining relative clauses.

prompt: Choose the correct relative word in a non-defining clause.
anchor: My brother, ___ wife is a surgeon, lives in London.
explanation: Correct answer: whose. Whose expresses possession in both defining and non-defining relative clauses. It connects my brother with his wife.

prompt: Choose the correct relative word for a place in a non-defining clause.
anchor: Paris, ___ we spent our honeymoon, is beautiful in spring.
explanation: Correct answer: where. Where means in which and introduces additional information about a place. That is not used in non-defining clauses.

prompt: Choose the correct relative word for a time in a non-defining clause.
anchor: Last December, ___ we visited Vienna, was unusually cold.
explanation: Correct answer: when. When refers to the time of the visit and introduces extra information. That cannot introduce a non-defining relative clause.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun referring to an entire preceding clause.
anchor: He forgot my birthday, ___ made me disappointed.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Which can refer to the entire preceding situation rather than a single noun. That cannot introduce this non-defining clause.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun referring to an entire preceding statement.
anchor: She passed all her exams, ___ surprised everyone.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Which refers to the fact that she passed all her exams. This is a non-defining relative clause.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after a comma.
anchor: The company hired a new director, ___ previously worked at Google.
explanation: Correct answer: who. Who is the subject of worked in a non-defining relative clause about a person. That is not allowed and whom cannot function as the subject.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a non-defining clause.
anchor: The museum, ___ opened in 1890, is being renovated.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Which introduces additional information about the museum. That cannot be used in non-defining relative clauses.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun that cannot be omitted.
anchor: The woman ___ called you is my manager.
explanation: Correct answer: who. Who is the subject of called and cannot be omitted. Relative pronouns can be omitted in defining clauses only when they function as objects.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun that can be omitted.
anchor: The film ___ we watched yesterday was excellent.
explanation: Correct answer: that. That functions as the object of watched and can be omitted in a defining relative clause. It cannot be omitted when it is the subject.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun that cannot be omitted.
anchor: The machine ___ produces these parts is very expensive.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Which acts as the subject of produces and therefore cannot be omitted.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun that can be omitted.
anchor: The person ___ I met at the conference works for Microsoft.
explanation: Correct answer: whom. Whom is the object of met. In a defining relative clause an object relative pronoun can be omitted.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun for a possessive relationship.
anchor: The student ___ essay won the prize is only sixteen.
explanation: Correct answer: whose. Whose expresses possession and cannot be omitted from this construction.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a formal construction.
anchor: The professor with ___ I collaborated has retired.
explanation: Correct answer: whom. Whom is used after a fronted preposition when referring to a person in formal English.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a formal construction.
anchor: The subject about ___ we were speaking is controversial.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Which refers to a thing and follows the preposition about in a formal relative clause.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a formal construction.
anchor: The building in ___ they work was constructed in 1920.
explanation: Correct answer: which. In which means where. The preposition in is already present so where would be incorrect in this construction.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a formal construction.
anchor: The reason for ___ he resigned remains unclear.
explanation: Correct answer: which. For which is a formal alternative to why. We cannot use for why in this construction.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a formal construction.
anchor: The year in ___ the company was founded was 1995.
explanation: Correct answer: which. In which is a formal alternative to when. The preposition in is already present.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after a quantifier.
anchor: She has three brothers, all of ___ live abroad.
explanation: Correct answer: whom. After all of we use whom when referring to people in a non-defining relative clause.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after a quantifier.
anchor: He bought five paintings, two of ___ were extremely expensive.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Two of which refers to two paintings out of the five mentioned. Which is used for things.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after a quantifier.
anchor: The company employs several engineers, none of ___ work remotely.
explanation: Correct answer: whom. None of whom is a formal relative construction referring to people.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after a quantifier.
anchor: They visited four cities, each of ___ had a different atmosphere.
explanation: Correct answer: which. Each of which refers individually to the four cities.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun after a quantifier.
anchor: The committee interviewed ten applicants, three of ___ were shortlisted.
explanation: Correct answer: whom. Three of whom refers to three people from the group of applicants.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a complex sentence.
anchor: The author, many of ___ books have become bestsellers, lives in Scotland.
explanation: Correct answer: whose. Many of whose books is a possessive relative construction. Whose connects the books to the author.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a complex sentence.
anchor: The company, the headquarters of ___ are in Zurich, operates worldwide.
explanation: Correct answer: which. The headquarters of which is a formal possessive construction referring to the company.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a complex sentence.
anchor: The scientist, ___ discoveries transformed modern medicine, received an award.
explanation: Correct answer: whose. Whose expresses possession and introduces a non-defining relative clause describing the scientist's discoveries.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a complex sentence.
anchor: The negotiations, during ___ several disagreements arose, lasted three days.
explanation: Correct answer: which. During which is a formal relative construction referring to the negotiations as a period or event.

prompt: Choose the correct relative pronoun in a complex sentence.
anchor: The proposal, the implications of ___ are still being discussed, may change the law.
explanation: Correct answer: which. The implications of which is a formal relative construction referring to the proposal. That cannot introduce a non-defining relative clause.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb to express present ability.
anchor: My younger sister ___ speak four languages fluently.
explanation: Correct answer: can. Can expresses present ability. Must expresses obligation or deduction. Should expresses advice and may expresses permission or possibility.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb to express general ability in the past.
anchor: When I was younger, I ___ run ten kilometres without stopping.
explanation: Correct answer: could. Could expresses general ability in the past. Can refers to present ability and will refers to the future.

prompt: Choose the correct expression for a successful action on one specific past occasion.
anchor: Although the exam was extremely difficult, she ___ pass it.
explanation: Correct answer: managed to. Managed to describes successful completion of a particular difficult action in the past. Could normally describes general past ability rather than a single successful achievement in an affirmative sentence.

prompt: Choose the correct expression for future ability.
anchor: After completing the course, you ___ develop your own applications.
explanation: Correct answer: will be able to. Can has no infinitive form and cannot normally follow will. Will be able to expresses future ability.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb for polite permission.
anchor: ___ I borrow your pen for a moment?
explanation: Correct answer: May. May I is a polite and relatively formal way of asking permission. Must expresses necessity and should expresses advice.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb to express a prohibition.
anchor: Visitors ___ enter this area without authorisation.
explanation: Correct answer: must not. Must not expresses prohibition. Do not have to and need not express a lack of obligation rather than prohibition.

prompt: Choose the correct expression to indicate that something is not necessary.
anchor: You ___ bring any food because everything is provided.
explanation: Correct answer: do not have to. Do not have to means an action is unnecessary. Must not and cannot can express prohibition. Should not expresses advice against an action.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb to express strong obligation.
anchor: You ___ wear a seat belt while driving.
explanation: Correct answer: must. Must expresses strong obligation. Might expresses possibility and could can express ability or possibility.

prompt: Choose the correct expression for an externally imposed obligation.
anchor: According to company policy, all employees ___ complete the safety training.
explanation: Correct answer: have to. Have to expresses an obligation imposed by rules or circumstances. The other options do not express the required obligation.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb to give advice.
anchor: You look exhausted. You ___ take a few days off.
explanation: Correct answer: should. Should is used to give advice or recommendations. Must not expresses prohibition and cannot expresses inability or impossibility.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression to give advice.
anchor: You ___ apologise for what you said yesterday.
explanation: Correct answer: ought to. Ought to expresses advice or moral obligation. Ought normally requires to before the infinitive. Must and should take the base verb without to.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb to express a weak possibility.
anchor: It is cloudy, so it ___ rain later this afternoon.
explanation: Correct answer: might. Might expresses uncertainty or possibility. Must indicates a much stronger deduction. Cannot expresses impossibility.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb for a possible future event.
anchor: The meeting ___ be postponed if the director is unavailable.
explanation: Correct answer: may. May expresses possibility. Must not expresses prohibition. Cannot expresses impossibility and ought requires to before the infinitive.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb for a logical deduction.
anchor: The lights are on and I can hear voices. Someone ___ be inside.
explanation: Correct answer: must. Must expresses a strong logical deduction based on evidence. Cannot would indicate the opposite conclusion.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb to express logical impossibility.
anchor: He ___ be at the office because I just saw him boarding a plane.
explanation: Correct answer: cannot. Cannot expresses a strong deduction that something is impossible or highly unlikely. Must would indicate certainty that he is there.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb for a polite request.
anchor: ___ you please open the window?
explanation: Correct answer: Could. Could you please is a conventional polite request. Must you can sound critical and may you is not the normal request construction.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb for a polite offer.
anchor: ___ you like some tea?
explanation: Correct answer: Would. Would you like is a standard polite expression for making an offer.

prompt: Choose the correct modal verb to express a hypothetical action.
anchor: If I had more free time, I ___ learn Italian.
explanation: Correct answer: would. Would plus the base verb expresses a hypothetical result in the second conditional.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a past habit.
anchor: When we were children, we ___ spend every summer at our grandparents' house.
explanation: Correct answer: would. Would can describe repeated habitual actions in the past. It does not normally describe past states in the same way.

prompt: Choose the correct expression for a past habit that no longer exists.
anchor: I ___ smoke cigarettes, but I stopped five years ago.
explanation: Correct answer: used to. Used to plus the base verb describes a past habit or state that is no longer true. Am used to requires a noun or -ing form and describes familiarity.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a strong past deduction.
anchor: The ground was wet this morning. It ___ rained during the night.
explanation: Correct answer: must have. Must have plus past participle expresses a strong deduction about the past. Must rained is ungrammatical.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an impossible past event.
anchor: She ___ stolen the money because she was abroad when it disappeared.
explanation: Correct answer: cannot have. Cannot have plus past participle expresses a strong conclusion that a past event was impossible.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an uncertain past event.
anchor: He is not answering his phone. He ___ forgotten to charge it.
explanation: Correct answer: might have. Might have plus past participle expresses an uncertain possibility about a past event.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a possible past event.
anchor: The package has not arrived. It ___ been sent to the wrong address.
explanation: Correct answer: may have. May have plus past participle expresses a possible explanation of a past event.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for criticism of a past action.
anchor: You ___ told me about the problem earlier. I could have helped.
explanation: Correct answer: should have. Should have plus past participle expresses criticism or regret about an action that did not happen.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a past mistake.
anchor: I ___ eaten so much before running. Now I feel terrible.
explanation: Correct answer: should not have. Should not have plus past participle expresses regret or criticism about an action that actually happened.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an unnecessary action that was performed.
anchor: You ___ bought any bread. I had already bought some.
explanation: Correct answer: need not have. Need not have plus past participle means the action happened but was unnecessary.

prompt: Choose the correct expression for an action that was unnecessary and did not happen.
anchor: We ___ pay for the tickets because admission was free.
explanation: Correct answer: did not have to. Did not have to expresses a lack of past obligation. Unlike need not have done, it does not imply that the action occurred.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an unreal past possibility.
anchor: If I had known you were in town, I ___ met you for coffee.
explanation: Correct answer: could have. Could have plus past participle expresses an unreal past possibility or opportunity.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an unreal past result.
anchor: If she had studied harder, she ___ passed the exam.
explanation: Correct answer: would have. Would have plus past participle expresses an imagined past result in the third conditional.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a strong past deduction.
anchor: He arrived completely exhausted after the marathon. He ___ been running for hours.
explanation: Correct answer: must have. Must have been running expresses a strong deduction about an ongoing activity in the past.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a negative past deduction.
anchor: The restaurant was closed all evening. They ___ served dinner there yesterday.
explanation: Correct answer: cannot have. Cannot have served expresses the conclusion that the past event was impossible.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a possible past explanation.
anchor: I cannot find my wallet. I ___ left it on the train.
explanation: Correct answer: might have. Might have left expresses an uncertain explanation of a past event.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a missed opportunity.
anchor: We ___ visited the museum, but we decided to stay at the hotel.
explanation: Correct answer: could have. Could have visited expresses an opportunity that existed but was not taken.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an expected past event that did not occur.
anchor: The train ___ arrived twenty minutes ago, but it is still delayed.
explanation: Correct answer: should have. Should have arrived expresses an expectation about an event that was supposed to happen by now.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a past obligation.
anchor: I ___ finish the report yesterday because my manager needed it urgently.
explanation: Correct answer: had to. Had to expresses past obligation. Must has no ordinary past tense form and must to is incorrect.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a future obligation.
anchor: Next month all employees ___ attend a mandatory training session.
explanation: Correct answer: will have to. Will have to expresses future obligation. Will must is ungrammatical because must cannot follow will.

prompt: Choose the correct expression for a future lack of obligation.
anchor: You ___ work tomorrow because the office will be closed.
explanation: Correct answer: will not have to. Will not have to expresses a future absence of obligation rather than prohibition.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for permission in the past.
anchor: When I was a child, I ___ stay up late on Saturdays.
explanation: Correct answer: was allowed to. Was allowed to expresses permission in the past. Will be able to expresses future ability rather than past permission.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for lack of permission.
anchor: Students ___ use their phones during the examination.
explanation: Correct answer: are not allowed to. Are not allowed to expresses prohibition. Do not have to and need not mean something is unnecessary.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a hypothetical past action.
anchor: If I had received your message, I ___ replied immediately.
explanation: Correct answer: would have. Would have replied expresses an unreal past result in the third conditional.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an uncertain past result.
anchor: If we had left earlier, we ___ avoided the traffic jam.
explanation: Correct answer: might have. Might have avoided expresses a possible rather than certain alternative past result.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a present deduction about an ongoing action.
anchor: I can hear music coming from her room. She ___ listening to something.
explanation: Correct answer: must be. Must be plus the -ing form expresses a strong deduction about an action happening now.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an uncertain ongoing action.
anchor: He is not at his desk. He ___ working from home today.
explanation: Correct answer: might be. Might be plus the -ing form expresses uncertainty about an action in progress.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an impossible ongoing action.
anchor: She ___ sleeping right now because I am speaking to her on the phone.
explanation: Correct answer: cannot be. Cannot be plus the -ing form expresses a strong conclusion that an ongoing action is impossible.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a past action that was unnecessary.
anchor: You ___ washed the car. It started raining immediately afterward.
explanation: Correct answer: need not have. Need not have washed means the car was washed but the action was unnecessary.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for criticism of a past omission.
anchor: You ___ checked the address before sending the package.
explanation: Correct answer: should have. Should have checked expresses criticism or regret about something that was not done.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for a strong negative deduction about the past.
anchor: He ___ finished the entire book in ten minutes. It has over a thousand pages.
explanation: Correct answer: cannot have. Cannot have finished expresses a strong deduction that the claimed past action was impossible.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an imagined present ability.
anchor: If I knew how to code in Python, I ___ automate this task.
explanation: Correct answer: could. Could expresses hypothetical ability in the second conditional.

prompt: Choose the correct modal expression for an imagined past obligation.
anchor: If I had accepted the management position, I ___ worked much longer hours.
explanation: Correct answer: would have had to. Would have had to expresses an unreal past obligation resulting from an imaginary past decision.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There are ___ students in the classroom today.
explanation: Correct answer: many. Many is used with plural countable nouns.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: We do not have ___ time before the train leaves.
explanation: Correct answer: much. Much modifies uncountable time.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: She has ___ friends in this city.
explanation: Correct answer: a few. A few indicates a small positive number of countable friends.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There is ___ milk left in the fridge.
explanation: Correct answer: a little. A little indicates a small positive amount of uncountable milk.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: He has very ___ patience with rude customers.
explanation: Correct answer: little. Little expresses an insufficient amount of uncountable patience.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: Very ___ people attended the lecture.
explanation: Correct answer: few. Few modifies plural countable people.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: Would you like ___ coffee?
explanation: Correct answer: some. Some is natural in polite offers with uncountable coffee.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: Do you have ___ questions about the lesson?
explanation: Correct answer: any. Any is common in neutral questions with plural countable nouns.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: We have not received ___ information yet.
explanation: Correct answer: any. Any is common in negative statements with uncountable information.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There are ___ apples in that basket.
explanation: Correct answer: several. Several modifies plural countable nouns.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: ___ of the two answers is correct. Both are wrong.
explanation: Correct answer: Neither. Neither means not one and not the other.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: ___ of these two routes will take you to the station. You can choose one.
explanation: Correct answer: Either. Either means one or the other of two alternatives.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: ___ of my parents are teachers.
explanation: Correct answer: Both. Both refers to two people together.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: ___ student must bring their own notebook.
explanation: Correct answer: Every. Every is followed by a singular countable noun.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: The teacher spoke to ___ student individually.
explanation: Correct answer: each. Each focuses on individual members of a group.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: ___ the students passed the exam. Not one failed.
explanation: Correct answer: All. All can modify the plural phrase the students.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: I have ___ money to buy the ticket.
explanation: Correct answer: enough. Enough indicates a sufficient quantity.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There is ___ sugar in this tea. I cannot drink it because it is too sweet.
explanation: Correct answer: too much. Too much indicates an excessive amount of uncountable sugar.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There are ___ cars on this narrow street. Traffic is terrible.
explanation: Correct answer: too many. Too many indicates an excessive number of countable cars.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There are ___ chairs for everyone to sit down.
explanation: Correct answer: enough. Enough indicates a sufficient number of chairs.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There is ___ water in the bottle to fill one glass.
explanation: Correct answer: enough. Enough indicates a sufficient amount of water.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: Only ___ participants completed the marathon.
explanation: Correct answer: a few. A few modifies plural countable participants.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: Only ___ progress was made during the meeting.
explanation: Correct answer: a little. A little modifies uncountable progress.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There is ___ chance of success without proper preparation.
explanation: Correct answer: little. Little expresses a small amount of the uncountable concept chance.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: ___ tourists visit the city every summer.
explanation: Correct answer: Many. Many is used with plural countable tourists.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: How ___ luggage are you taking?
explanation: Correct answer: much. Luggage is uncountable and takes much.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: How ___ suitcases are you taking?
explanation: Correct answer: many. Suitcases are plural countable items.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: ___ of the information was inaccurate.
explanation: Correct answer: Some. Some can modify uncountable information.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: I did not understand ___ of what he said.
explanation: Correct answer: much. Much refers to a large proportion of an uncountable amount of speech.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: She ate ___ of the cake but left a slice for me.
explanation: Correct answer: most. Most of the cake refers to the greater part of a specific cake.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: ___ of the three proposals was accepted.
explanation: Correct answer: None. None can refer to zero members of a group of three.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: ___ of the two candidates has the required experience.
explanation: Correct answer: Neither. Neither refers to not one of two candidates.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There is hardly ___ bread left.
explanation: Correct answer: any. Hardly any means almost none and can modify uncountable bread.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: We have ___ more work to do before Friday.
explanation: Correct answer: a lot of. A lot of can modify uncountable work.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: He has ___ books about medieval history.
explanation: Correct answer: a lot of. A lot of can modify plural countable books.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.
anchor: There are ___ reasons to reconsider the decision.
explanation: Correct answer: numerous. Numerous modifies plural countable reasons.

prompt: Choose the correct quantifier.

explanation: Correct answer: safest. Safe forms the superlative by adding st because it already ends in e.

prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.
anchor: He is the ___ person I have ever met.
explanation: Correct answer: most generous. Longer adjectives usually take most in the superlative.

prompt: Choose the correct superlative adjective.
anchor: That was the ___ mistake in the entire report.
explanation: Correct answer: biggest. Big doubles the final consonant before adding est.

prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.
anchor: This is the ___ option available within our budget.
explanation: Correct answer: cheapest. Cheap is a one-syllable adjective and normally takes est.

prompt: Choose the correct irregular comparative.
anchor: This restaurant is ___ than the one we visited yesterday.
explanation: Correct answer: better. Good has the irregular comparative better and superlative best.

prompt: Complete the irregular comparative.
anchor: The weather today is ___ than yesterday.
explanation: Correct answer: worse. Bad has the irregular comparative worse and superlative worst.

prompt: Choose the correct irregular superlative.
anchor: That was the ___ performance of the evening.
explanation: Correct answer: best. Best is the irregular superlative of good.

prompt: Complete the irregular superlative.
anchor: This is the ___ result we have obtained so far.
explanation: Correct answer: worst. Worst is the irregular superlative of bad.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative of little.
anchor: I have ___ free time than I did last year.
explanation: Correct answer: less. Less is the comparative of little for uncountable quantities such as time.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: She has ___ responsibilities than her manager.
explanation: Correct answer: fewer. Fewer is used with plural countable nouns such as responsibilities.

prompt: Choose the correct superlative quantifier.
anchor: This option requires the ___ amount of money.
explanation: Correct answer: least. Least is the superlative used with an uncountable quantity such as money.

prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.
anchor: Of all the teams ours made the ___ mistakes.
explanation: Correct answer: fewest. Fewest is the superlative used with plural countable nouns.

prompt: Choose the correct irregular comparative.
anchor: She has ___ experience than the other applicants.
explanation: Correct answer: more. More is the comparative of much and many and works with uncountable experience.

prompt: Complete the irregular superlative.
anchor: This department has the ___ employees in the company.
explanation: Correct answer: most. Most is the superlative of many and much.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative adverb.
anchor: She speaks English ___ than her brother.
explanation: Correct answer: more fluently. Adverbs ending in ly normally form the comparative with more.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: He drives ___ than his colleagues.
explanation: Correct answer: more carefully. Most ly-adverbs form the comparative with more.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative adverb.
anchor: She finished the race ___ than expected.
explanation: Correct answer: faster. Fast functions as an adverb and forms the comparative with er.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: The new system operates ___ than the old one.
explanation: Correct answer: more efficiently. The comparative of the adverb efficiently is more efficiently.

prompt: Choose the correct irregular comparative adverb.
anchor: She performed ___ than anyone expected.
explanation: Correct answer: better. Well has the irregular comparative better.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: He arrived ___ than the other participants.
explanation: Correct answer: earlier. Early changes y to i before the comparative ending er.

prompt: Choose the correct superlative adverb.
anchor: Of all the candidates she answered ___ .
explanation: Correct answer: most confidently. Longer ly-adverbs normally form the superlative with most.

prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.
anchor: He completed the task ___ of all the employees.
explanation: Correct answer: most efficiently. The superlative of efficiently is most efficiently.

prompt: Choose the correct irregular superlative adverb.
anchor: Among the finalists she performed ___ .
explanation: Correct answer: best. Well has the irregular superlative best.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: The train travels ___ than the bus.
explanation: Correct answer: more quickly. Quickly normally forms the comparative with more.

prompt: Choose the correct equality comparison.
anchor: This laptop is ___ expensive as that one.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Equality comparisons use as plus adjective plus as.

prompt: Complete the equality comparison.
anchor: She is ___ intelligent as her sister.
explanation: Correct answer: as. As intelligent as expresses equal degree.

prompt: Choose the correct negative equality form.
anchor: This exam is not ___ difficult as the previous one.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Not as plus adjective plus as expresses a lower degree.

prompt: Complete the equality comparison.
anchor: He works just ___ hard as his colleagues.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Just as hard as emphasises equal degree.

prompt: Choose the correct equality structure.
anchor: The new apartment is twice ___ large as the old one.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Twice as plus adjective plus as expresses a multiplicative comparison.

prompt: Complete the equality comparison.
anchor: This suitcase is half ___ heavy as mine.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Half as heavy as expresses a ratio of one half.

prompt: Choose the correct comparison.
anchor: The journey took three times ___ long as expected.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Three times as long as compares durations multiplicatively.

prompt: Complete the equality comparison.
anchor: The second proposal is almost ___ effective as the first.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Almost as effective as expresses a degree close to equality.

prompt: Choose the correct comparison.
anchor: This explanation is nowhere near ___ clear as the original.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Nowhere near as plus adjective plus as emphasises a large difference in degree.

prompt: Complete the equality comparison.
anchor: The results were not nearly ___ good as we had hoped.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Not nearly as good as means considerably worse than expected.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative modifier.
anchor: The new version is ___ more reliable than the previous one.
explanation: Correct answer: much. Much can intensify a comparative adjective. Very cannot normally directly modify more reliable in this structure.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: This problem is ___ easier than it first appeared.
explanation: Correct answer: far. Far intensifies a comparative and indicates a substantial difference.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative modifier.
anchor: The second test was ___ more difficult than the first.
explanation: Correct answer: slightly. Slightly modifies a comparative to indicate a small difference.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: The new policy is ___ less restrictive than the old one.
explanation: Correct answer: considerably. Considerably intensifies a comparative and indicates a large difference.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative modifier.
anchor: The latest model is ___ more expensive than its predecessor.
explanation: Correct answer: a bit. A bit can modify comparatives to express a small difference.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: The situation became ___ worse after the announcement.
explanation: Correct answer: even. Even can intensify a comparative such as worse.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative modifier.
anchor: The revised proposal is ___ better than the original.
explanation: Correct answer: significantly. Significantly modifies a comparative and expresses a meaningful difference.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: The second candidate was ___ more experienced than the first.
explanation: Correct answer: substantially. Substantially can intensify a comparative adjective.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative modifier.
anchor: This explanation is ___ clearer than the previous one.
explanation: Correct answer: a little. A little modifies a comparative and indicates a small improvement.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: The project proved ___ more complex than anticipated.
explanation: Correct answer: far. Far more complex is a natural intensified comparative.

prompt: Choose the correct double comparative.
anchor: The weather is getting ___ and ___ .
explanation: Correct answer: colder and colder. Repeating a comparative with and expresses gradual change.

prompt: Complete the double comparative.
anchor: The situation is becoming ___ and ___ complicated.
explanation: Correct answer: more. More and more complicated expresses a continuing increase in complexity.

prompt: Choose the correct double comparative.
anchor: The city is becoming ___ .
explanation: Correct answer: more and more crowded. More and more plus adjective expresses progressive change.

prompt: Complete the double comparative.
anchor: The longer we waited the ___ impatient we became.
explanation: Correct answer: more. The plus comparative followed by the plus comparative expresses a linked change.

prompt: Choose the correct correlative comparative.
anchor: The harder you work the ___ your results become.
explanation: Correct answer: better. The harder the better is a correlative comparative expressing a relationship between two changes.

prompt: Complete the correlative comparative.
anchor: The more you practise the ___ mistakes you make.
explanation: Correct answer: fewer. Fewer is used with countable plural mistakes in a correlative comparative.

prompt: Choose the correct correlative comparative.
anchor: The more information we collect the ___ our predictions become.
explanation: Correct answer: more accurate. The more information the more accurate expresses a relationship between increasing data and accuracy.

prompt: Complete the correlative comparative.
anchor: The less time we have the ___ efficiently we must work.
explanation: Correct answer: more. The less time the more efficiently is a correlative comparative structure.

prompt: Choose the correct correlative comparative.
anchor: The higher the price the ___ the demand tends to be.
explanation: Correct answer: lower. The higher the lower expresses an inverse relationship between two quantities.

prompt: Complete the correlative comparative.
anchor: The sooner we start the ___ we will finish.
explanation: Correct answer: earlier. The sooner the earlier links two comparative outcomes.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative structure.
anchor: This solution is superior ___ the previous one.
explanation: Correct answer: to. Superior is followed by to rather than than in standard English.

prompt: Complete the comparison.
anchor: Her experience is inferior ___ that of the other candidates.
explanation: Correct answer: to. Inferior takes the preposition to.

prompt: Choose the correct comparison.
anchor: This approach is preferable ___ the alternative.
explanation: Correct answer: to. Preferable is normally followed by to when comparing alternatives.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: The new model is different ___ the previous version.
explanation: Correct answer: from. Different from is the standard form in both British and American English. Different than also occurs in American English but is not the intended choice here.

prompt: Choose the correct comparison.
anchor: She is senior ___ me in the organisation.
explanation: Correct answer: to. Senior meaning higher in rank is followed by to rather than than.

prompt: Complete the comparison.
anchor: He is junior ___ the department manager.
explanation: Correct answer: to. Junior meaning lower in rank takes the preposition to.

prompt: Choose the correct comparison.
anchor: The final result was comparable ___ our earlier findings.
explanation: Correct answer: to. Comparable to expresses similarity between results. Comparable with can also be used but is not among the options.

prompt: Complete the comparison.
anchor: This method is more effective ___ the traditional approach.
explanation: Correct answer: than. Ordinary comparative adjectives formed with more are followed by than when making a direct comparison.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative structure.
anchor: The new software is less reliable ___ its predecessor.
explanation: Correct answer: than. Less plus adjective is followed by than in comparisons.

prompt: Complete the comparison.
anchor: Her salary is higher ___ mine.
explanation: Correct answer: than. Higher is a comparative adjective and normally takes than.

prompt: Choose the correct superlative structure.
anchor: This is one of the ___ important discoveries of the decade.
explanation: Correct answer: most. One of the plus superlative plus plural noun identifies a member of an exceptional group.

prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.
anchor: She is by far the ___ qualified candidate.
explanation: Correct answer: most. By far can intensify a superlative. The most qualified means the candidate has the highest qualification level.

prompt: Choose the correct superlative form.
anchor: It was the ___ challenging assignment I had ever received.
explanation: Correct answer: most. The most plus adjective forms the superlative of longer adjectives.

prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.
anchor: This is easily the ___ solution we have considered.
explanation: Correct answer: best. Easily can intensify a superlative and best is the irregular superlative of good.

prompt: Choose the correct superlative structure.
anchor: Of the three proposals this is the ___ expensive.
explanation: Correct answer: least. The least plus adjective forms the negative superlative and identifies the lowest degree among three or more alternatives.

prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.
anchor: He is the second ___ experienced member of the team.
explanation: Correct answer: most. The second most plus adjective ranks someone immediately below the highest position.

prompt: Choose the correct superlative structure.
anchor: This is the third ___ city in the country.
explanation: Correct answer: largest. The third largest expresses a rank within a group using an ordinal number and superlative.

prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.
anchor: That was one of the ___ decisions the committee had to make.
explanation: Correct answer: hardest. One of the plus superlative plus plural noun expresses membership in a group of extreme examples.

prompt: Choose the correct superlative form.
anchor: This is the ___ convincing argument presented so far.
explanation: Correct answer: most. The most convincing is the superlative of convincing.

prompt: Complete the superlative sentence.
anchor: The northern region receives the ___ rainfall of all.
explanation: Correct answer: most. Most is the superlative of much and can modify uncountable rainfall.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative expression.
anchor: The new system is ___ as reliable as the old one.
explanation: Correct answer: twice. Twice as plus adjective plus as expresses a multiplicative comparison.

prompt: Complete the comparative expression.
anchor: The apartment costs three times ___ much as mine.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Three times as much as compares amounts multiplicatively.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative structure.
anchor: This project is no ___ difficult than the previous one.
explanation: Correct answer: more. No more difficult than means that the degree of difficulty does not exceed that of the comparison item.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: The revised figures are all the ___ surprising given the economic situation.
explanation: Correct answer: more. All the more plus adjective expresses an increased degree caused by a particular circumstance.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative structure.
anchor: The problem is not so much technical ___ organisational.
explanation: Correct answer: as. Not so much A as B expresses that B is a more accurate description than A.

prompt: Complete the comparative expression.
anchor: The proposal is more expensive ___ it is effective.
explanation: Correct answer: than. More adjective than clause can compare two qualities or degrees within the same proposal.

prompt: Choose the correct comparative structure.
anchor: The new findings are ___ more significant than previously assumed.
explanation: Correct answer: all the. All the more plus adjective emphasises an increased degree of importance or significance.

prompt: Complete the comparative sentence.
anchor: The situation is becoming increasingly ___ .
explanation: Correct answer: unstable. Increasingly directly modifies the positive form of an adjective. Increasingly more unstable is usually redundant.

prompt: Choose the correct advanced comparison.
anchor: The results were far ___ convincing than the researchers had hoped.
explanation: Correct answer: less. Far less plus adjective expresses a substantial reduction in degree compared with expectations.

prompt: Complete the advanced comparative structure.
anchor: The more thoroughly the data are analysed the ___ reliable the conclusions become.
explanation: Correct answer: more. The more thoroughly the more reliable is a correlative comparative expressing a relationship between analytical thoroughness and reliability.

prompt: Choose the correct negative inversion.
anchor: Never before ___ such an extraordinary performance.
explanation: Correct answer: have I witnessed. When never before begins a clause it triggers subject auxiliary inversion. The present perfect is appropriate for experience up to the present.

prompt: Complete the sentence using negative inversion.
anchor: Rarely ___ such dedication among new employees.
explanation: Correct answer: have we seen. Rarely at the beginning of a clause triggers inversion of the auxiliary and subject.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted structure.
anchor: Seldom ___ an opportunity of this magnitude.
explanation: Correct answer: does a company receive. Seldom triggers subject auxiliary inversion. Present simple requires does with the singular subject a company.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: Under no circumstances ___ confidential information be disclosed.
explanation: Correct answer: should. Under no circumstances triggers inversion and should be disclosed forms a modal passive construction.

prompt: Choose the correct negative inversion.
anchor: At no point ___ that the project would be cancelled.
explanation: Correct answer: did they suggest. A fronted negative expression triggers inversion with did plus the base verb in past simple.

prompt: Complete the sentence using negative inversion.
anchor: Little ___ how serious the situation had become.
explanation: Correct answer: did he realise. Little meaning hardly at all triggers inversion when placed at the beginning of a clause.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted form.
anchor: Nowhere else ___ such a combination of cultures.
explanation: Correct answer: will you find. Nowhere else is a negative locative expression and triggers subject auxiliary inversion.

prompt: Complete the sentence using negative inversion.
anchor: Not once ___ responsibility for the failure.
explanation: Correct answer: did the director accept. Not once triggers inversion with did and the base form accept.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted structure.
anchor: On no account ___ the emergency exit be blocked.
explanation: Correct answer: must. On no account is a negative expression triggering inversion. Must be blocked is a modal passive structure.

prompt: Complete the sentence using negative inversion.
anchor: In no way ___ these results prove the original hypothesis.
explanation: Correct answer: do. In no way triggers inversion. Present simple with the plural subject these results uses do.

prompt: Choose the correct inversion after only after.
anchor: Only after the investigation ended ___ the full extent of the damage.
explanation: Correct answer: did we understand. Only after followed by an introductory time clause triggers inversion in the main clause.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: Only when the results were published ___ the mistake.
explanation: Correct answer: did the researchers notice. Only when at the beginning triggers inversion in the main clause rather than the subordinate clause.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted structure.
anchor: Only by working together ___ solve this problem.
explanation: Correct answer: can we. Only by plus a gerund triggers inversion in the following main clause.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: Only then ___ how much we had underestimated the risks.
explanation: Correct answer: did we realise. Only then at the beginning triggers subject auxiliary inversion.

prompt: Choose the correct inversion.
anchor: Only in exceptional circumstances ___ the deadline be extended.
explanation: Correct answer: may. Only plus a restrictive adverbial at the beginning triggers inversion. May be extended is a modal passive construction.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: Only after several attempts ___ to access the database.
explanation: Correct answer: were they able. Only after at the beginning triggers inversion in the main clause. Were they able expresses past ability.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted form.
anchor: Only once the contract had been signed ___ the work begin.
explanation: Correct answer: could. Only once introduces a restrictive time clause and the main clause uses inversion with the modal could.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: Only through substantial investment ___ the infrastructure be modernised.
explanation: Correct answer: can. Only through a restrictive phrase triggers inversion in the main clause. Can be modernised is passive.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted structure.
anchor: Only after the meeting ___ the seriousness of the problem.
explanation: Correct answer: did she appreciate. Only after at the beginning requires inversion in the main clause.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: Only when all the evidence had been examined ___ a verdict.
explanation: Correct answer: did the jury reach. Only when triggers inversion in the main clause and did takes the base verb reach.

prompt: Choose the correct structure after not until.
anchor: Not until midnight ___ the rescue operation.
explanation: Correct answer: did they complete. Not until at the beginning triggers inversion in the main clause.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: Not until the final chapter ___ the identity of the murderer.
explanation: Correct answer: does the reader discover. Not until triggers inversion in the main clause. Present simple with singular reader uses does.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted structure.
anchor: Not until the following morning ___ what had happened.
explanation: Correct answer: did he learn. Not until at the beginning triggers subject auxiliary inversion in the main clause.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: Not until the documents were released ___ the public become aware of the scandal.
explanation: Correct answer: did. Not until triggers inversion and past simple uses did plus the base verb become.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted structure.
anchor: Not until years later ___ the importance of her discovery.
explanation: Correct answer: was it recognised. Not until triggers inversion. The passive past simple requires was plus past participle recognised.

prompt: Choose the correct correlative inversion.
anchor: No sooner had the meeting started ___ the fire alarm went off.
explanation: Correct answer: than. No sooner is paired with than and usually triggers inversion with past perfect when fronted.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: Hardly had we arrived ___ it began to rain.
explanation: Correct answer: when. Hardly had plus past participle is commonly followed by when to describe two events occurring in quick succession.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted structure.
anchor: Scarcely ___ the speech when the audience began applauding.
explanation: Correct answer: had she finished. Scarcely at the beginning triggers inversion and past perfect is commonly used before when.

prompt: Complete the sentence using inversion.
anchor: No sooner ___ the announcement than the markets reacted.
explanation: Correct answer: had they made. No sooner at the beginning triggers inversion with past perfect and is followed by than.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted structure.
anchor: Hardly ___ the door when the telephone rang.
explanation: Correct answer: had he closed. Hardly at the beginning triggers past perfect inversion to express an event immediately preceding another.

prompt: Choose the correct conditional inversion.
anchor: ___ I known about the delay I would have left later.
explanation: Correct answer: Had. Had I known is an inverted third conditional equivalent to if I had known.

prompt: Complete the conditional inversion.
anchor: ___ you require further assistance please contact our office.
explanation: Correct answer: Should. Should you require is a formal conditional inversion equivalent to if you should require.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted conditional.
anchor: ___ I in your position I would reject the offer.
explanation: Correct answer: Were. Were I in your position is a formal inverted second conditional equivalent to if I were in your position.

prompt: Complete the conditional inversion.
anchor: ___ the company invested earlier it would have avoided the crisis.
explanation: Correct answer: Had. Had the company invested is an inverted third conditional equivalent to if the company had invested.

prompt: Choose the correct conditional inversion.
anchor: ___ the situation to deteriorate further additional measures would be necessary.
explanation: Correct answer: Were. Were the situation to deteriorate is a formal hypothetical conditional equivalent to if the situation were to deteriorate.

prompt: Complete the conditional inversion.
anchor: ___ any problems arise during installation contact technical support.
explanation: Correct answer: Should. Should any problems arise is a formal conditional equivalent to if any problems should arise.

prompt: Choose the correct inverted conditional.
anchor: ___ it not been for your help we would have failed.
explanation: Correct answer: Had. Had it not been for is an inverted third conditional expressing an unreal past circumstance.

prompt: Complete the conditional inversion.
anchor: ___ the proposal to be accepted substantial changes would be required.
explanation: Correct answer: Were. Were the proposal to be accepted is a formal hypothetical conditional with a passive infinitive.

prompt: Choose the correct conditional inversion.
anchor: ___ you change your mind the offer will remain open until Friday.
explanation: Correct answer: Should. Should you change your mind is a formal alternative to if you change your mind.

prompt: Complete the conditional inversion.
anchor: ___ the warning been taken seriously the accident might have been prevented.
explanation: Correct answer: Had. Had the warning been taken seriously is a third conditional with past perfect passive and inversion.

prompt: Choose the correct inversion after so.
anchor: So difficult ___ the examination that only a few students passed.
explanation: Correct answer: was. When so plus adjective is fronted for emphasis the verb is inverted before the subject.

prompt: Complete the emphatic inversion.
anchor: So rapidly ___ the technology develop that regulations could not keep pace.
explanation: Correct answer: did. So plus adverb at the beginning triggers inversion. Past simple uses did plus base verb develop.

prompt: Choose the correct inversion after such.
anchor: Such ___ the demand that tickets sold out within minutes.
explanation: Correct answer: was. Such was the demand is an emphatic inverted structure followed by a result clause with that.

prompt: Complete the emphatic inversion.
anchor: So severe ___ the storm that all flights were cancelled.
explanation: Correct answer: was. So plus adjective triggers inversion with the verb be and the singular subject storm.

prompt: Choose the correct emphatic inversion.
anchor: Such ___ the complexity of the problem that no immediate solution was possible.
explanation: Correct answer: was. Such was the complexity is an emphatic inverted structure followed by a that-clause expressing the result.

prompt: Choose the correct cleft sentence.
anchor: It was the director ___ approved the final proposal.
explanation: Correct answer: who. An it-cleft sentence uses it was plus the focused element plus a relative clause. Who refers to the director as a person.

prompt: Complete the cleft sentence.
anchor: It was in 2015 ___ the company expanded internationally.
explanation: Correct answer: that. An it-cleft can emphasise a time expression using it was plus the time plus that-clause.

prompt: Choose the correct wh-cleft structure.
anchor: What we need ___ a more transparent decision-making process.
explanation: Correct answer: is. A wh-cleft sentence uses what plus clause followed by be to highlight the required information.

prompt: Complete the emphatic sentence.
anchor: The reason ___ she resigned was the lack of professional opportunities.
explanation: Correct answer: why. The reason why plus clause is a common structure for focusing attention on an explanation.

prompt: Choose the correct emphatic do structure.
anchor: I ___ understand your concerns but I disagree with your conclusion.
explanation: Correct answer: do. Emphatic do can be added to an affirmative present simple sentence to strengthen the statement.
